land.text: Qatna sacked by Suppiluliuma I after the palace was burned in 1340 BC; the Hittite shape of -1300 is the first to reach the Orontes

successors.note: The hittites dossier (me-04-a) has Qatna in its 'syrian-city-states' gain of -1345; this dossier dates the final sack to between 1340 and 1334. The site was then 'uninhabited for about three centuries'.

capitals.name: Qatna (Tell al-Mishrifeh)
capitals.note: The page puts the tell in Homs Governorate 'about 18 km from Homs'; the coordinates are approximate, north-east of Homs.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Qatna. The page describes the kingdom as running 'from the upper Orontes valley west to Qadeš' with Palmyra 'its easternmost city' and Yamhad on the north, and gives no area (the city itself: 110 ha at the start of the Middle Bronze). The shape (80 km round Homs plus 40 km round Palmyra, about 22,500 km2) is the researcher's reading. At its height under Ishhi-Addu (attested 1783-1778 BC) it ruled the Beqaa, Damascus-oasis cities and coastal Amurru kingdoms (undated) and Hazor 'dominated the south'; these are not drawn.

ledger.note: c. 2000 BC: the Amorite kingdom of Qatna is established. 'In the Middle Bronze, the Kingdom of Qatna was established around 2000 BC'; the site was first occupied in the Late Chalcolithic IV (3300-3000 BC). A round number, not a founding act.

ledger.note: 16th century BC: Qatna becomes a Mitannian vassal. 'It became a Mitannian vassal in the 16th century BC'; the page says it kept some autonomy into the 14th century. Mid-century is a convention.

ledger.note: c. 1446 BC (bridged): Mitanni's hold ends as Egypt's begins. The page has no end for the Mitannian vassalage; Thutmose III 'reached Qatna during his eighth Asiatic campaign, c. 1446 BC' and 'established vassalage ties', and the Thutmose III page puts the Euphrates crossing in his regnal year 33 and makes no mention of Qatna.

ledger.note: c. 1446 BC: Thutmose III makes Qatna an Egyptian vassal. 'Thutmose III reached Qatna during his eighth Asiatic campaign, c. 1446 BC, and established vassalage ties'; Amenhotep II later 'fought troops from Qatna near the city' in his seventh regnal year (undated). Akizzi still wrote to Akhenaten c. 1334 BC.

ledger.note: c. 1337 BC (bridged): Qatna falls to Hatti while its king Akizzi pleads with Egypt (letter EA 55, 'before the death of Akhenaten, to whom the letter was addressed, in c. 1334 BC'); the sack falls between the palace's destruction in 1340 BC and the letter.

region.text: the upper Orontes valley round Homs west to Qadesh, with Palmyra 'its easternmost city' and Yamhad to the north (the page gives no boundary)

ledger.note: c. 1337 BC: Suppiluliuma I sacks Qatna. 'The final sack of Qatna occurred after the royal palace was destroyed in 1340 BC', attributed to Suppiluliuma I who came with Aziru of Amurru. The Suppiluliuma I page lists Qatna among the kingdoms he conquered across the Euphrates, with no year; his reign is 'c. 1350-1322 BC'.

region.text: the upper Orontes valley round Homs west to Qadesh, with Palmyra 'its easternmost city' and Yamhad to the north (the page gives no boundary)

ledger.note: c. 1337 BC: the kingdom of Qatna ends. The tell is then 'uninhabited for about three centuries', reoccupied in the late 10th century BC and destroyed by the Assyrians in 720 BC (Aramean phase, not drawn).

wars.name: Yamhad's invasion of Qatna
wars.outcome: 'In the late 17th century BC, Yamhad invaded and defeated Qatna during the reign of Yarim-Lim III'; the Yamhad page has Qatna 'remained independent, then made peace with Yamhad under Yarim-Lim III'. No vassalage is recorded.
wars.note: Year is the middle of the late 17th century; the Yamhad page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yamhad) dates Yarim-Lim III 'in the mid-17th century BC'.

wars.name: Thutmose III's eighth campaign
wars.outcome: Egypt 'established vassalage ties' with Qatna; no territory changes owners.
wars.note: The Thutmose III page does not name Qatna; its eighth campaign is regnal year 33 across the Euphrates.

notes: Cliopatria has no Qatna. The dates rest almost entirely on the Qatna page (the Suppiluliuma I and Thutmose III pages are silent on Qatna's year). Not drawn: the Beqaa, Hazor, the coastal Amurru kingdoms and the Damascus-oasis cities (Apum) as Qatna's vassals under Ishhi-Addu (c. 1783-1778 BC), because the page dates none of them; Idanda's Hittite vassalage (undated, before the first Syrian war); Nuhashshe's possible absorption of Qatna in the 14th century (disputed); Parga near Hamath, 'occupied for a while' and retaken by Sumu-Epuh. The Mitanni vassalage end (1446) is bridged, as the page implies Mitanni kept some control into the 14th century while Egypt also held vassalage ties. The hittites dossier's -1345 'syrian-city-states' gain should be read with this dossier's -1337 for Qatna. Page budget: four pages.
